executive_summary: Indo Count’s September recovery combines core mix improvement with rapidly scaling utility bedding and brands. The useful evidence is broader than the PAT rebound: new businesses contribute around 30% of income, all three US utility plants exceed 65% utilization, and management now expects to exceed FY27 revenue/margin guidance.
research_stance: Constructive operating evidence, with valuation and insurance/working-capital reconciliation still important after the sharp share-price rise.
results_analysis: September 2026 consolidated sales were ₹1,673.00 crore, +57.5% YoY and +38.6% QoQ. PAT was ₹132.00 crore, +238.5% YoY and +109.5% QoQ. These percentage changes use the rounded local dataset, so small differences from company-exact growth percentages are expected.

Local operating profit was ₹233.00 crore and OPM 14.00%, compared with 10.00% a year earlier and 12.00% in June 2026. PAT margin was 7.89%. OPM is the dataset’s operating-profit/sales measure, not automatically management-adjusted EBITDA or a segment EBIT margin.

The call uses total income ₹1,699 crore and EBITDA ₹259 crore/15.3%, while the local table uses sales ₹1,673 crore and operating profit ₹233 crore/14%. The ₹26 crore other-income bridge explains most of the EBITDA numerator difference; do not call the 14% local OPM an EBITDA miss. The Bhilad inventory loss ₹45.02 crore is matched by an equivalent insurance receivable/exceptional credit, so it is not extra recurring operating growth. Interim insurance payment ₹14.99 crore was approved after quarter-end, with final recovery still open.

FY26 annual CFO was ₹573 crore and free cash flow ₹372 crore. These are annual figures, not September-quarter cash flow. Latest balance-sheet borrowings were ₹1,314 crore at 2026-09-30; gross borrowings must not be confused with call net debt. Snapshot ROCE 8.19% is an older-period return measure, not a freshly recomputed quarterly return.

business_economics: The core bed-linen franchise, US utility bedding and branded/licensed products have different unit economics. Group revenue growth therefore mixes core meters/realizations and newly scaling businesses; a single EBITDA margin cannot prove each newer investment has reached mature profitability.

The call’s₹1,699cr total income includes₹26cr above local operating sales. The EBITDA numerator difference is also₹26cr. On consistent arithmetic,₹259/₹1,699 is15.24% while₹233/₹1,673 is13.93%; mixing the numerator from one and denominator from the other creates a false operating signal.
earnings_quality: The reported Bhilad inventory loss/insurance receivable is a separate earnings-and-cash matter. Recognition of a receivable can offset the accounting loss before full cash collection. The reported recovery should not be treated as additional recurring operating earnings or assumed fully liquid.

Four-to-five months input inventory can cushion a cost increase before customer repricing, but it also ties up cash and can create exposure when prices reverse. Management says past increases were passed through; the audit treats that as company commentary and continues to test cash conversion and future realized margins.
capital_allocation: All three utility plants above65% utilization indicate progress, not completion. The return test is whether higher utilization translates into segment contribution after labor, logistics, brand/licensing and financing costs, with cash conversion rather than revenue alone.

The₹8,000cr CY2028 ambition does not require new growth capacity per management, yet₹250cr maintenance/compliance and other projects remain planned over12–18months. A credible investment case must charge those existing commitments and working capital even if no new growth plant is needed.
valuation_logic: Use separate core and new-business assumptions and then reconcile net debt, leases and contingent items. No valid enterprise value follows from the unreconciled generic₹1,314cr borrowings minus disclosed cash: it does not reproduce management₹518cr net debt.

The base case should use supported margin commentary and a staged capacity ramp; the bull case needs new-business returns converging toward core economics; the bear case combines weaker US demand, slower inventory turns and lower margins. Do not build the analyst’s20% margin aspiration into a management-guided target.
peer_positioning: Welspun is a direct export/home-textile comparison but has flooring, different US onshore exposure and its own Vapi disruption. Trident and yarn manufacturers are not exact substitutes for branded/utility bedding economics. Compare business-level returns, working-capital requirements and customer concentration before valuation multiples.
